prs.title: Keep a pure return type inference filtered by its constraint in a recursive call resolution
prs.author: colinhacks
prs.body:
Since #64311, a re-entrant call resolution skips constraint checks, which also skips filtering a pure return type inference by its constraint. The re-entrant result is the one the declaration keeps, so the type argument can end up outside its constraint with no error. This keeps the filter in the re-entrant pass.

Fixes #64529

prs.title: Fix moduleResolution -> customConditions test to actually apply both conditions
prs.author: auvred
prs.body:
`webpack, browser` string is splitted by `,`

tsc/internal/tsoptions/commandlineparser.go#L363

and later isn't trimmed

tsc/internal/tsoptions/commandlineparser.go#L367

However, enum options, like `lib` are trimmed

tsc/internal/tsoptions/commandlineparser.go#L381

---

Other string-list options are passed without spaces (https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2FTypeScript+path%3A%2F%5Etsc%5C%2Ftestdata%5C%2Ftests%5C%2Fcases%5C%2F%2F+%2F%5C%2F%5C%2F%5Cs*%40%28types%7CtypeRoots%29.*%2C.*%2F&type=code) so I thought this is the intended way, and this is enough to fix this on test-case level

---

Aside:

```
> tsc --noEmit --showConfig --customConditions 'webpack, browser' --lib 'es2015, dom'
{
    "compilerOptions": {
        "customConditions": [
            "webpack",
            " browser"
        ],
        "lib": [
            "es6",
            "dom"
        ],
        "noEmit": true
    },
    "files": [
        "./index.ts"
    ]
}
```

See how `--lib` trims space and correctly produces `["es6", "dom"]` while `--customConditions` has `["webpack", " browser"]`. Should I open a separate issue for this?

prs.title: Cache inferences made from type arguments
prs.author: ahejlsberg
prs.body:
With this PR we cache inferences made from type arguments of references to the same alias or class/interface. The PR supersedes #64388 which implements similar caching, but does so through a separate cache instead of leveraging the existing `invokeOnce` caching infrastructure.

The PR fixes an issue with the existing cache where `priority`, `contravariant`, and `bivariant` states weren't included in the cache key. This would cause false matches and lead to dropped inferences. This fix revealed a test case in `correlatedUnions.ts` that incorrectly depended on dropped inferences and now requires use of `NoInfer<T>`. The issue can be observed by the error in [this version](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?#-LZAmgSAQMlhsrlNJ87sxwbwcIEuCQmHCEXkmgJNBFpGg5r1uuQoKoQnYLsgYYxjvTCGigbUAD60sTMpiMvw81nAgTHYKqK4CIA) of the test that simply reverses the declaration order of `letter` and `caller` in the `LetterCaller` type.

Thanks @a-tarasyuk for researching the root cause and fix for the issue in #64378.

Fixes #64378.

prs.title: [api] Ensure completion symbols returned to API always come from the current snapshot
prs.author: andrewbranch
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/64518#discussion_r4137953063:

> This is actually just a more obvious symptom of an existing bug. In main, every completion symbol from the temporary snapshot get registered by the parent snapshot's `snapshotData` record. That means the caller can get completions, assume the returned symbols belong to the current snapshot, and use the current snapshot's checker on them. If the symbol being operated on is transient, that will probably cause incorrect results or a crash.
>
> If an API method is going to return objects from a new snapshot, that new snapshot must be returned to the client as well, so the objects can be operated on. `getCompletionsAtPosition` only _optionally_ includes symbols, and only advances the snapshot if auto-imports are both needed for the position and not already prepared. Whether or not to include auto-imports ever should be configurable, but currently is not by the API.
>
> A proper fix needs to address this from a few angles:
>
> * Be able to configure auto-imports in the API (perhaps per call, definitely by applying user preferences to a snapshot)
> * Be able to create a snapshot that is prepared to auto-import a file
>
> I think with both of those, you can keep `getCompletionsAtPosition`'s return value as is and not have it return a snapshot, or bifurcate the method into one variant that returns a snapshot and one that doesn't:
>
> * If `includeSymbols` is false, use the same logic that exists today,
…(truncated)

prs.title: Generate compiler option definitions, create JSON schema
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
For the new website playground, I need some sort of spec for our `CompilerOptions`. In Strada, this was done by parsing out at runtime our internal options declarations and turning that into a website UI and JSON schema (if we remembered to do it), which then would eventually get sent over to schemastore (if we remembered to do it...), and then eventually make it into VS Code etc (if we remembered to do it........).

Instead, let's just define our options as metadata like we do the AST and other stuff, then code generate all of the Go code, TS code, and even our own JSON schema files. #54192 is a long-open issue requesting that we ship a JSON schema with the package, so, this PR also adds that file to the package too so `node_modules/typescript/schemas/tsconfig.schema.json` is now valid. Eventually, we can use this in our VSIX, I think, though historically that one's been more permissive of dead options.

A good bonus is that we can now codegen `CompilerOptions.Clone`, `parseCompilerOptions`, the transpile options clearing func, and more.

Fixes #54192
